# The refusals

Every code the engine answers with when it does not do what it was
asked, and what each means. The list is written from the engine's own
constants, so it has every code and no other.

A refusal has four parts.

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| the code | one of the words below; it never changes, so a program or an agent can act on it |
| the place | the variable, or the place in the class definition, that the refusal is about, such as `/access/update` |
| the message | what happened, in words, for a person |
| the hint | often, what to do about it |

The same word can appear in more than one list: `forbidden` is always
about who may, wherever it comes from.

## Refusals of a call

What a call is answered with when the engine does not carry it out: a create, a set, a transition, a read. Nothing is written when a command is refused.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unknown_class` | No class of that name. |
| `unknown_document` | No current document with that id, no such version in its history, or a document the caller may not see, who is answered in the same words (ADR-0049). |
| `unknown_table` | No explicit table of that name. |
| `unknown_variable` | A value names a variable or a field the class does not have. |
| `read_only` | A value is given for a computed variable. |
| `required` | A required input is blank. |
| `bad_value` | A value is not of the variable's type, or an argument is malformed. |
| `not_in_values` | A text is outside the variable's enum list (ADR-0023). |
| `out_of_range` | A number is outside the variable's min and max (ADR-0034), or a text is longer than the database's text limit (ADR-0021). |
| `too_many_elements` | A composite value has more than the hard cap of ADR-0013. |
| `key_reused` | The idempotency key was used with a different command (ADR-0026). |
| `duplicate` | A document with that id exists already, or a table or view name is taken. |
| `not_supported` | A construct the design has that this build does not implement yet. |
| `closed` | The store is closed. |
| `storage` | The database refused a statement; Message carries its words. |
| `bad_formula` | A filter's where does not parse or bind; Pos says where. |
| `not_allowed` | A function class a filter may not use, a SQL statement the endpoint refuses, or At on a command that writes (ADR-0042). |
| `too_many_rows` | A SQL statement returns more than MaxSQLRows. |
| `unknown_blob` | A File names a hash the blob store does not hold, or a size that differs from the stored one (ADR-0033). |
| `blob_too_large` | A file exceeds the database's blob limit. |
| `terminal` | The document is in a terminal state and cannot change (ADR-0039). |
| `stateless` | Create or CreateMany on a class without states, a stateless application that stores no documents (ADR-0040). |
| `unknown_transition` | The class has no named transition of that name (ADR-0040). |
| `wrong_state` | The transition exists and does not leave the document's state. |
| `guard_false` | The transition's guard did not evaluate TRUE; an erroring guard is FALSE. |
| `too_many_transitions` | More than eight transitions fired by themselves after one command, eventless or timed (ADR-0008, ADR-0047). |
| `forbidden` | The caller may not do this. A rule of the class refused it (ADR-0049), or the right of a variable in the document's state (ADR-0041), or the work is for a system group the caller is not in (ADR-0052), or the caller acts for somebody and no substitution says it may (ADR-0053). The path, or the variable, names which. |
| `reason_required` | A content administrator's command gets past a rule and gives no reason (ADR-0052, item 4). The path is the place of the rule. |
| `too_deep` | An action was queued by a chain of actions deeper than MaxActionDepth (ADR-0044); its row is written dead. |
| `unknown_action` | No action of the outbox has that key, or the database has no action of that name. |
| `unknown_parameter` | An argument names a parameter the action's definition does not have (ADR-0045). |
| `not_registered` | The action is defined and nothing in this process implements it: its Go function was not given to Open (ADR-0027). |
| `action_error` | The Go function of an action returned an error, or panicked; Message carries its words. A function that returns an error of the store keeps that error's code. |
| `bad_result` | What an action returned does not fit what its definition declares under returns. |
| `outbound_off` | The action is sent as an HTTP request and this process sends none: it was opened without Options.Outbound (ADR-0045, item 7). |
| `unknown_connection` | The host program gave this process no connection of that name. |
| `host_not_allowed` | The outbound rules of this process do not let a request go to that host, over that scheme or port, or to the address it resolves to; or the host is not one of the request's connection. |
| `secret_unavailable` | The host program did not supply a secret a request reads. No answer: the request is tried again. |
| `no_reply` | A request got no reply: the receiver was not reached, or did not answer in time. Tried again. |
| `try_later` | The receiver answered 408, 429 or 5xx. Tried again, no sooner than the reply's Retry-After asks. |
| `refused` | The receiver answered with a status that is neither a success nor a request to try again. A refusal. |
| `not_ok` | The receiver answered 2xx and the definition's ok is not TRUE for the reply. A refusal. |
| `reply_too_large` | The reply is larger than the outbound rules read. |
| `unknown_row` | A table.update addresses a row the table does not have (ADR-0044). |

## Findings in a definition

What the engine reports when it checks a class, a table, a schema or an action before defining it. Every finding of a definition is reported at once, each with its place in the definition.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bad_json` | The definition is not the JSON the class format expects. |
| `missing` | A required element is absent or empty. |
| `bad_name` | A name is not an identifier, or uses the reserved separator or suffix. |
| `reserved_name` | A name the generated tables use, or a keyword. |
| `duplicate` | A name declared twice, in any case. |
| `unknown_type` | A type the type system does not have. |
| `unknown_schema` | An object or rows type names a schema that is not defined. |
| `schema_cycle` | A schema contains itself. |
| `too_deep` | Objects nest more than MaxObjectDepth deep. |
| `not_allowed` | A property that this kind of variable, field or element may not have. |
| `bad_formula` | A formula does not parse or bind; Pos says where. |
| `type_mismatch` | A formula's type is not the variable's. |
| `not_a_condition` | A guard, rule condition or access rule is not bool. |
| `cycle` | Computed variables depend on each other in a loop. |
| `unknown_state` | A reference to a state the class lacks. |
| `unknown_variable` | A reference to a variable the class lacks. |
| `unknown_transition` | A reference to a transition the class lacks. |
| `unknown_class` | An action names a class the database does not have (ADR-0044). |
| `unknown_table` | An action names a table the database does not have (ADR-0044). |
| `unknown_action` | A rule names an action that has no definition (ADR-0045). |
| `unknown_parameter` | A rule gives an action a parameter its definition does not have (ADR-0045). |
| `unknown_secret` | A request names a secret its connection does not declare (ADR-0045). |
| `unknown_connection` | A definition names a connection the host program did not give this process (ADR-0045). |
| `bad_trigger` | A trigger of a triggered variable is malformed. |
| `bad_value` | An enum value, a range bound or a literal is wrong. |
| `rule_left_out` | A note and no refusal. The class leaves an access rule out; it is accepted, and nobody but a content administrator passes that rule (ADR-0052, item 5). |
| `too_many_columns` | A generated table would exceed MaxColumns. |
| `not_supported` | A construct the format allows that the engine does not implement yet. |

## Errors of a formula

What a formula stops with when it cannot give a value. Inside a commit the refusal carries this code and names the variable whose formula failed.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `div_by_zero` | A division by zero. IFERROR says what to answer instead. |
| `not_a_number` | An operation whose result is not a number, such as the square root of a negative number. |
| `bad_text` | A text that does not read as the number, the date or the value a function was asked to take from it. |
| `out_of_range` | A value outside what a function or a type takes: a position below 1, a date the calendar does not have, a text past the size limit. |
| `length_mismatch` | Two lists of different lengths where a function needs them equal. |
| `too_many_elements` | A list with more elements than the limit allows. |
| `query_failed` | A lookup or a query that could not be answered. |
| `overflow` | An exact number too large for its type. |
| `inexact` | An exact value that cannot be kept at the scale asked without losing digits. |
| `currency_mismatch` | Money of two currencies in one operation. |
